name: Visual Studio Code
purpose: A free code editor that runs Python, notebooks and Git in one place. You can use another editor if your lab prefers one.
version_guidance: Install the current stable release, not Insiders.

windows.text: Download Visual Studio Code for your system from code.visualstudio.com and install it.
Open it, go to Extensions, and install the Python extension published by Microsoft.
Open your project folder, then run "Python: Select Interpreter" from the Command Palette and choose your .venv.

macos.text: Download Visual Studio Code for your system from code.visualstudio.com and install it.
Open it, go to Extensions, and install the Python extension published by Microsoft.
Open your project folder, then run "Python: Select Interpreter" from the Command Palette and choose your .venv.

linux.text: Download Visual Studio Code for your system from code.visualstudio.com and install it.
Open it, go to Extensions, and install the Python extension published by Microsoft.
Open your project folder, then run "Python: Select Interpreter" from the Command Palette and choose your .venv.

windows.expected: Three lines: a version number such as 1.x.y, a commit code and your processor type

macos.expected: Three lines: a version number such as 1.x.y, a commit code and your processor type

linux.expected: Three lines: a version number such as 1.x.y, a commit code and your processor type

common_problems.solution: In VS Code, open the Command Palette and run "Shell Command: Install 'code' command in PATH", then open a new terminal.

common_problems.problem: VS Code runs the wrong Python
common_problems.solution: Run "Python: Select Interpreter" again and pick the one inside your .venv folder.

manual_review: The code --version check and the macOS PATH fix are standard VS Code behavior, not quoted from the pages read.
